template.name: Website builder
template.description: Design and build a website or web app, tested in a real browser. Each task is a branch and a pull request, reviewed on GitHub.

stages.name: Build
stages.description: The change is in a pull request, tested in the browser, with screenshots in its description.

lead.title: Lead
lead.instructions:
## Coding rules
- You never write app code.
- Keep tasks small: one task = one branch = one PR. Give each task the files it may edit and a clear done-when.
- Design tasks come before the build tasks that use them.

designer.title: Designer
designer.instructions:
- Design the pages the task asks for in code (HTML/CSS or the project's components), following the frontend-design skill.
- Keep to the project's look unless the task says otherwise; explain your choices in the PR.

developer.title: Developer
developer.instructions:
- Build what the task asks for, on its own branch, and open a pull request titled [TASK-ID] Short title.
- Check your change in a browser and follow the accessibility-checklist skill before opening the PR.

qa.title: QA
qa.instructions:
- Test what was built against its done-when in a real browser, with the webapp-testing skill. Try the unhappy paths.
- For each problem: steps to reproduce, what you expected, what happened, a screenshot.

files.skills/accessibility-checklist/SKILL.md:
---
name: accessibility-checklist
description: "Use before opening or approving a pull request that changes a page: the accessibility checks it must pass."
---

# Accessibility checklist

Check every page your change touches:

- Everything works with the keyboard alone: Tab reaches each control in a sensible order, focus is always visible, Escape closes dialogs.
- Text contrast is at least 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text and icons that carry meaning).
- Every image has alt text (empty alt="" for decoration); every form field has a visible label.
- Headings go in order (one h1, then h2…), and links say where they go.
- Nothing flashes, and animations respect prefers-reduced-motion.
- The page still works at 200% zoom and 320px wide.

Note what you checked in the PR description.
